features.description: Novel PDF ingestion — a source document becomes chapter-addressed, citable text: PyMuPDF extraction + chapter detection + overlapping sentence-aligned chunks whose offsets resolve back to the source. Serves M1 (provenance) and M7 (the receipt). See project_context.md 5.4.
features.evidence: 2026-07-25 (s7): 32 tests green (20 chunking + 10 PDF reader + 2 e2e). Adapted from patchy631/ai-engineering-hub/notebook-lm-clone (MIT, verified by reading LICENSE at the repo ROOT — the prior BACKLOG claim of 'no license' had only checked the subdirectory). THREE upstream defects fixed, each with a regression test: (1) SILENT DATA LOSS — upstream advanced with `start = max(start + chunk_size - overlap, end)`, which skips past `end` whenever the sentence snap retreats further than the overlap covers; test_upstream_advance_rule_would_drop_characters reproduces the arithmetic and proves characters vanish, then proves ours covers everything. The precise trigger condition is `start + chunk_size - overlap > end`, i.e. short sentences relative to the window — the first fixture (84-char sentences, 20-char overlap) did NOT trigger it and the proof test correctly failed until the fixture was corrected. (2) QUOTE/OFFSET DISAGREEMENT — upstream stripped chunk text but recorded unstripped offsets, so text[char_start:char_end] != quote; trimming now moves the offsets with it. (3) PAGE-RELATIVE -> CHAPTER-RELATIVE offsets: decisive rather than cosmetic, because the spoiler guard gates on chapter and a page number cannot answer 'has this been revealed yet?'. DESIGN CALL: a PDF with no detectable chapter headings RAISES instead of degrading to one chapter — stamping every fact chapter=1 leaves the guard running and its tests green while silently making the whole novel visible to every character from turn one. allow_single_chapter=True is the explicit opt-in. Its RETRIEVAL path was rejected outright: vector_db.search(query_vector, top_k) applies no epistemic filter and would form a second unguarded read path beside store.visible_to(). E2E proves the whole chain: real PDF -> PyMuPDF -> chunk -> Provenance -> on-disk SQLite -> engine restart -> source document RE-READ FROM DISK -> offsets still resolve, plus the guard still gates the ingested facts by chapter.

features.description: Knowledge propagation — knower_scope is derived from Scene.witnesses, so presence at a scene confers knowledge and absence does not. Closes the unbuilt half of KB-13 and makes project_context.md 4.2 (the acceptance condition) hold across turns.
features.evidence: 2026-07-25 (s7): 24 tests green (18 unit + 6 integration against a real on-disk store with restarts). THE INVARIANT: propagation is MONOTONIC — it may add a knower or move an acquisition earlier, never remove a knower or delay one. Two consequences that are easy to get wrong and are both tested: (1) an UNTRACKED fact stays untracked — is_visible reads knower_scope=None as 'visible to everyone once revealed', so attaching a scene's witnesses would take a fact from visible-to-all down to visible-to-three, the exact inverse of learning; witnesses_learn is therefore a no-op there and start_tracking exists for the deliberate narrowing case. (2) earliest acquisition wins — someone who learned a secret at ch3 does not re-learn it at ch7, or a replay would show them ignorant of what the audience watched. Monotonicity is ALSO enforced at the store boundary (CanonStorePort.record_learning), not just in the domain, because losing a knower is silent at read time: the scene still renders, just with someone who has forgotten. Learning is deliberately NOT routed through supersede — a claim's truth is unchanged when someone learns it, and superseding would close a validity window nothing invalidated. Found while building: FactRow.knower_scope was annotated list[str] but has always stored list[dict]; corrected to match VectorRow.

features.description: The turn loop — PlaythroughService: assemble the actor's filtered view, apply a choice to world state, propagate knowledge from who was present, render one scene. Plus replay_as (project_context.md 8.1) and the citation receipt. Covers M2/M3/M6/M7/S3.
features.evidence: 2026-07-25 (s7): 10 tests green. E2E plays FIVE choices against a real on-disk store, reopens it, and asserts the acceptance condition per character: Dexter knows the secret from ch1, Doakes learns it at ch4 (the turn he was in the room), Deborah was present at turn 2 but NOT at the disclosure and never learns it, Rita was present later and never learns it, the AUDIENCE is never told. Then replay_as('deb') re-renders the SAME branch and asserts the secret is absent from her citations — the demo's whole claim, mechanically checked. Exactly ONE model call per turn and it decides nothing: every state transition is computed in code first, because the guarantee comes from what is absent from the assembled context, not from instructing a model to withhold. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED by running the real demo: the fallback narrator recited the player's upcoming CHOICE LABELS as prose, because the prompt template renders both known facts and options as '- ' bullets and the line scan could not tell them apart — three lines below a prompt instruction saying never to name them. Fixed by scoping the scan to the knowledge block that ends at 'RULES:', with a regression test. A second, related sloppiness: the template's empty-knowledge placeholder was also a '- ' bullet and parsed as a fact named 'Nothing'; it is now parenthesised prose, because a placeholder is not a fact.

features.description: The demo is runnable end to end from a terminal against the real novel: `story-engine play` seeds canon from Darkly-Dreaming-Dexter-1.pdf, plays choices, shows the receipt, and replays the branch as another character.
features.verification: uv run story-engine play --auto --turns 5 --replay-as deborah --db data/interim/verify.db
features.evidence: 2026-07-25 (s7): runs clean. Seeds 5 canon facts whose quotes are SLICED FROM THE PDF AT SEED TIME rather than pasted into source — a pasted quote can drift from its offsets through one transcription slip, and a drifted citation still looks exactly like a good one. Every anchor carries a must_contain sentinel so re-ingestion that moves offsets fails loudly at seed time instead of quietly citing the wrong paragraph. Observed contrast, which IS the demo: as Dexter, turn 0 narrates the Dark Passenger and Harry's code with 3 facts withheld; as Deborah, the same turn 0 of the same branch reads 'stands at the edge of the moment with nothing to go on' with 10 facts withheld. Cast uses NOVEL names (Deborah, not Debra) per FANFIC-05 and project_context.md 6.4. No API key required: ScriptedLLM replays authored beats and composes a deliberately mechanical fallback otherwise, so the stage demo cannot be broken by a timeout or an unlucky sample.
